original_value: This study investigates two‐way relaying where an energy harvesting capable relay exchanges information between two sources. Legitimate information is wire‐tapped by an eavesdropper. To intercept wire‐tapping, this study exploits a friendly jammer. Secrecy outage analysis of the energy harvesting two‐way relaying network with the friendly jammer over Rayleigh fading channels is first proposed in terms of individual secrecy outage probabilities and then validated by computer simulations. Various results demonstrate the efficacy of the jammer in preventing the eavesdropper from stealing the source information and significant impacts of relay location, jammer location, jammer's transmit power, energy conversion efficiency, time switching ratio on the security performance.

result.paraphrase: This study examines two-way relaying in which an energy-harvesting relay exchanges information between two sources. A wiretapper intercepts the legitimate information, and a friendly jammer is used to counter the interception. It first proposes secrecy-outage analysis for the energy-harvesting two-way relaying network with a friendly jammer over Rayleigh fading channels, using individual secrecy-outage probabilities, and then confirms the results through computer simulations. The findings show the jammer effectively prevents the eavesdropper from stealing the source information, and that relay location, jammer location, jammer transmit power, energy conversion efficiency, and the time-switching ratio all significantly affect security performance.
